articles.image_title: Argentinien: A dentist provides free medical attention to a patient during a 24-hour ''Japanese-style strike'' organized by the Faculty of Dentistry of the University of Buenos Aires (FOUBA) at Plaza Houssay in Buenos Aires, Argentina, on April 15, 2026. Students, teachers, and non-teaching staff offer free dental, medical, and legal services for 24 consecutive hours to protest against the national government's budget cuts and to advocate for the implementation of the University Financing Law. articles.title: Z+ (abopflichtiger Inhalt); Tabak in Großbritannien: Großbritannien hat genug vom Tod durchs Rauchen
articles.teaser: Es ist das härteste Nichtraucherschutzgesetz der Welt: Die Briten verbieten Schritt für Schritt den Verkauf von Tabak. Deutschland ist dazu noch lange nicht bereit.
articles.image_title: Tabak in Großbritannien: epa10899624 A young person smokes in London, Britain, 04 October 2023. British Prime Minister Sunak said that MPs will be given a free vote in parliament on rising the age at which people can buy cigarettes and tobacco in England by one year every year so that eventually no-one can buy them. Under the plan, everyone who is 14 or younger today in 2023, will not legally be able to buy cigarettes ever during their lives. The UK government will also consider restricting the sale of disposable vapes and change the packaging of the devices to tackle the rising rates of children and young people using them. EPA/TOLGA AKMEN
